title: The Last Ticket
logline: In a long queue for tickets, a traveller near the front watches the board change just before his turn, and the seat he wanted is gone.
human_question: What does the last, ordinary minute of not getting what you wanted actually feel like?

situation.what_happens: A queue forms for a limited number of seats on a journey many people want to make on the same day. The wait develops its own small society: complaints, phone calls, people holding places for others. Somewhere in the middle of it the supply runs out, and the news travels backwards along the line. Those near the front who miss it by a few places take it hardest, and then have to decide what to do with the rest of the day.
situation.who_is_involved: Travellers whose reasons for the journey have nothing in common: a holiday, a funeral, a job, an obligation that cannot be moved; the staff who spend the day saying no; people queuing on someone else's behalf.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For each traveller, something different and mostly invisible to everyone else, from a day out to being present for something that will not wait. For the staff, delivering a refusal they did not cause. This is exactly why the film cannot treat the queue as one appetite with one face.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Queues like this build, peak and dissolve within a few hours, and the refusal arrives as an ordinary administrative fact rather than as a confrontation. What follows varies: waiting for the next one, paying more elsewhere, arguing, giving up, going home. Nothing about the refusal can be arranged, and it must never be provoked or announced in advance.

concept_merge.why_together: C005 contributes both halves of the source's own distinction: ordinary spending and pleasure trips are listed among the everyday occasions of greed-rooted minds, and the same act done out of need or practical wisdom is explicitly not counted as unwholesome. In one queue, both are standing in line and cannot be told apart. C006 contributes the fact that the queue is also made of two kinds of wanting, one that rose on its own and one that somebody else pressed on the person, and the refusal falls on both in exactly the same way.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the group's subject has been running quietly under something as unremarkable as waiting for a seat, and that the wall it meets is not dramatic at all: a board changes. It also shows why the sources' distinction by aim is not a way of sorting a crowd. Nobody in the line can be placed from outside, and the film must not try.

concept_links.why: Spending on what we like and going on pleasure trips are among the source's everyday occasions for greed-rooted minds [C005-M:L5] [C005-M:L7], and the same source is equally explicit that an act done out of need or practical wisdom is not counted as unwholesome [C005-M:L9]. A queue holds both, which is the point; the digest also notes that the source does not say what kind of mind those excluded cases are instead, so the film must not fill that gap.

Some travellers queue unprompted, out of habit and expectation, while others are pushed to try by a friend or by a family's need; the sources count both as wanting and treat prompting as including one's own coaxing of a hesitating mind [C006-M:L5] [C006-P:L44]. The refusal makes no distinction between them.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Wanting can be as ordinary as hoping for a seat on a train, and whether it rose on its own or somebody pushed us to try, a changing board can end it in a second. Not everyone in the queue is wanting in the same way, and nobody watching can tell which is which.
what_must_be_real: A real queue on a real day, and travellers' own unscripted reactions. No refusal staged, anticipated aloud, or provoked, and no one interviewed in the minute it lands on them.
position_hint: closing candidate: the group's first refusal, deliberately small and administrative, so that the wall arrives without a villain behind it.
risks: Treating everyone in the queue as an instance of the same thing
The scene feeling arranged if the refusal is anticipated rather than found
Filming people at a moment they would not have chosen
drop_if: No genuine refusal can be part of the film without staging or provoking it
Travellers cannot consent freely at the moment it happens

connections.note: Hope bought in small daily doses there, hope refused all at once here.
Two refusals: one delivered by a system that meant nothing by it, one by another person wanting the same thing more.

selection.reason: The group's turn into refusal, at the smallest possible scale and with the source's own exclusion for need kept intact.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
